extraction.name: CADS-dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale collection of 22,022 CT volumes with voxel-level annotations covering 167 anatomical structures for whole-body CT segmentation. The dataset aggregates data from over 40 diverse sources spanning 16 countries and more than 100 medical centers, including public archives, medical imaging challenges, and newly acquired clinical data. It supports development of whole-body segmentation models and broader medical imaging research.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by aggregating CT scans from three main source categories: (1) large-scale public archives including TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, and AbdomenCT-1K; (2) specialized annotation collections from medical imaging challenges (Grand Challenge, MICCAI) and focused research studies (Han-Seg, SAROS, TCIA); and (3) newly contributed images comprising 484 anonymized head CTs from Istanbul Medipol University and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans from TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar. Selection criteria focused on CT scans covering key anatomical regions throughout the body. Approximately 79% of the initial collection had no manual annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 21% of the 22,022 CT volumes (4,695 volumes) contain any annotations at collection time, with annotations typically confined to a single organ system. The remaining 79% lack any manual annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CT volumes from over 40 sources including: TotalSegmentator dataset (1,203 annotated volumes), National Lung Screening Trial (NLST, 7,172 scans), CT-RATE (3,134 scans), AbdomenCT-1K (1,062 scans), The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), Grand Challenge and MICCAI challenge datasets, Han-Seg, SAROS, VISCERAL Gold and Silver Corpus, KiTS, LiTS, BTCV-Abdomen, BTCV-Cervix, CHAOS, VerSe, and various TCGA and CPTAC collections. Additionally, 484 newly acquired anonymized head CTs from Istanbul Medipol University and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans (CT-TRI) from TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-stage annotation pipeline combining human and automated methods. Three in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist manually annotated 10 additional structures (spinal canal, larynx, heart chambers, and other radiotherapy-critical structures) on VISCERAL Gold Corpus images. Brain structure annotations were generated by registering Han-Seg CT scans with the SimNIBS MRI atlas using ANTs non-rigid transformation. SAROS dataset sparse 2D slice annotations were interpolated to dense 3D volumes. Quality control of pseudo-labels used shape-based outlier detection via neural implicit functions, excluding the lowest-scoring 10% of pseudo-labels. Expert radiation oncologist (5.5 years in practice) reviewed segmentation outputs for clinical acceptability via slice-by-slice review. Test set annotations from TotalSegmentator dataset were reviewed by in-house medical professionals who classified each of 104 structures as reliable or unreliable.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For test set quality review, in-house medical professionals independently assessed all 104 anatomical structures in 65 TotalSegmentator test images, classifying annotations as reliable or unreliable with documented error descriptions; unreliable structures were excluded from final evaluation. For model flavor selection, statistical tests (Shapiro-Wilk normality, Levene variance equality, then ANOVA/Welch's ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis with post-hoc Tukey's HSD or Dunn's test) were applied to Dice and HD95 scores to rank three model flavors per structure, with the highest-ranked flavor's pseudo-label selected as the final label.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net framework (specialized models for 9 anatomical groups) for pseudo-label generation; neural implicit functions / auto-decoder for shape-based pseudo-label quality control; ANTs (Advanced Normalization Tools) non-rigid registration for brain structure annotation from SimNIBS MRI atlas; vesselFM foundation model for rib costovertebral joint retrieval; MIM software for reference annotation generation in hospital cohort
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The shape-based quality control exclusion strategy may eliminate cases involving pathological conditions that present atypical anatomical variations, potentially limiting the model's ability to learn clinically important edge scenarios; existing automated labeling approaches introduce known systematic errors in complex anatomical structures like ribs and vertebrae, which models trained on such data learn and propagate
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited training data for certain structures (e.g., buccal mucosa appears in less than 1,000 scans with only 30 ground-truth annotations); very small organs (volumes below 0.5 mL) where standard CT resolution limits and partial volume effects impact accuracy; the brain mask currently includes all central nervous components within the skull, which may be too inclusive for certain applications; the optic chiasm tends to be under-segmented; the heart segmentation omits superior portions; the rectum appears shorter than its anatomical extent; the trachea is currently limited to air content without surrounding tracheal wall; vena cava needs more precise delineation; due to privacy considerations, facial features are intentionally anonymized, limiting applications requiring detailed facial analysis; dataset spans only from head to knees, excluding hands and feet; vascular structures are often absent in current datasets due to annotation complexity
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and model are intended to advance robust AI solutions in radiology and make comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers; clinical potential spans radiation oncology (streamlining treatment planning through rapid organ delineation), diagnostic radiology (enabling automated organ volume quantification and detection of subtle anatomical changes), and large-scale population studies; expert radiation oncologists validated predicted segmentations as clinically reliable for precision therapeutic planning
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Newly acquired hospital head CT scans are anonymized; a Gaussian filter (σ=5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing) is applied to facial regions of newly acquired hospital head CT scans to obscure patient identity; the 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans are described as anonymized; ethical approval was obtained for the release of new head CT scans and abdominal CT scans
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of whole-body CT segmentation models; radiation treatment planning through rapid organ delineation; automated organ volume quantification and detection of subtle anatomical changes in diagnostic radiology; large-scale population studies; anatomical landmark detection; cross-modality registration for CT-MRI fusion and PET-CT alignment; anatomy-guided image reconstruction for radiation dose reduction; longitudinal organ tracking; personalized anatomical modeling; body composition analysis
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Oversampling was applied during CADS-model training by assigning sampling weights based on the inverse probability of class occurrence to address class imbalance across 167 anatomical structures (e.g., less frequent cervical vertebrae C1-C5 received higher sampling weights). Targeted training subsets were created for specialized anatomical regions (e.g., images with adequate head coverage selected for brain and head-and-neck models). Pseudo-labeling was used to propagate annotations across unlabeled scans via iterative self-training with three complementary model flavors (GT-flavor, Pseudo-flavor, Shape-flavor). Brain structure annotations were generated by registering Han-Seg CT scans with the SimNIBS MRI atlas using ANTs non-rigid transformation. SAROS sparse 2D slice annotations were interpolated between annotated slices to create dense 3D per-slice annotations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All images were reoriented to the standard RAS (Right-Anterior-Superior) convention, resampled to a uniform 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and affine transformation matrices were simplified by removing rotation and translation components while preserving only scaling and shear. For patient privacy in newly acquired hospital head CT scans, a Gaussian filter (sigma=5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing) was applied to facial regions. Pseudo-labels identified as low-quality via shape-based outlier detection (90th-percentile Hausdorff distance) were excluded from training (lowest-scoring 10% removed). Head structure pseudo-labels were filtered by predicted brain voxel count (scans below 2,000 voxels excluded) and spatially cropped to remove false-positive predictions outside the head region. Rib segmentation was refined through connected components analysis with majority voting for consistent labeling, and costovertebral joints were retrieved using a tubular structure detection model with morphological opening and size filtering (100-1,500 voxels). For model training, image intensities were scaled from the 5th to 95th percentiles to the range [0,1] with clipping for contrast enhancement. Annotation inconsistencies in TotalSegmentator test set ground truth labels were corrected through expert review of 65 test images, with unreliable annotations excluded from evaluation.
